title: Ishan Kishan's 270 in Duleep Trophy Final Caps Remarkable Comeback From BCCI Exile
excerpt: The East Zone captain scored a monumental 270 against South Zone after spending two years outside India's squad, saying he freed his mind from overthinking to focus solely on scoring runs.
body:
• Ishan Kishan scored 270 in the Duleep Trophy final for East Zone against South Zone, his highest first-class score.
  • The wicketkeeper-batsman lost his BCCI central contract in 2023 and spent nearly two years rebuilding through domestic cricket.
  • Kishan credits his turnaround to clearing his mind of overthinking and expectations, saying his job as a batsman is simply to "watch the ball and react."
  • He scored hundreds in the Ranji Trophy 2025-26 and helped Jharkhand win the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy with 517 runs including two centuries before regaining his BCCI contract.

A Monumental Knock

Ishan Kishan produced an epic 270 in the Duleep Trophy final, leading East Zone against South Zone in what he described as the most visible manifestation of an inner transformation forged through two difficult years away from international cricket. The innings was the highest of Kishan's first-class career and announced his return to red-ball relevance in emphatic fashion.

"I didn't actively try to change myself. It just happened naturally," Kishan said in the post-day press conference. "When I was out of the squad, I realized that we ultimately only have one job to do: simply to score runs. That is the only thing that helps you in your career."

From All-Format Player to Contract Loss

In 2023, Kishan was an all-format player for India. A trail of unforeseen events — including an extended absence from domestic cricket that drew BCCI scrutiny — culminated in him losing his central contract entirely. The fall was swift and public for a player who had been part of India's T20 and ODI squads.

Rather than retreat, Kishan threw himself into domestic cricket. He scored hundreds in the Ranji Trophy during the 2025-26 season and helped Jharkhand win the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, accumulating 517 runs with two centuries. The BCCI contract and a place in white-ball formats followed.

"Any other thoughts will only manipulate your mindset, push you into overthinking, and pile on unnecessary pressure. Our job is to step in and win matches for the team. That's all you should care about."

— Ishan Kishan

The Mental Reset

Kishan described his approach as deliberately free of calculation. "The best thing I'm doing nowadays is not thinking about anything. My job as a batsman is just to go there, watch the ball, and react to it and not keep any expectations from myself," he said.

Coming into the final after a string of T20 matches, Kishan spent time at the BCCI Centre of Excellence practicing specifically with the red ball. He acknowledged that the transition from white-ball cricket required adjustment — in his first Duleep Trophy innings against North East Zone, he was caught between playing a shot and leaving, getting out to indecision.

For the final, he stripped back his game plan to its simplest form: keep adding 50-run partnerships. "A lot of things factor in — picking up when their bowlers are tiring, when they are opening up the field — so you keep batting around these things without worrying about the result," he explained.

Growth Through the Grind

Asked whether the step down to domestic cricket was difficult after playing in front of roaring crowds and flashing cameras, Kishan said the experience was genuinely valuable.

"When we play regularly for the Indian team, you just keep playing in a flow. You might be a very good player, which is why you're playing for India, but your growth stagnates at a certain point," he said. "So when you take one step back and go back to domestic cricket, you start from zero again."

The 270 in the Duleep Trophy final suggests that Kishan's reset has produced results that go beyond mere survival. For a player who once seemed destined to be a permanent fixture in India's white-ball setup, the red-ball masterclass may have opened a new dimension in his career — one built on patience and clarity rather than explosiveness alone.
nri_angle: Kishan's comeback resonates with the Indian cricket community worldwide as a story of perseverance through the BCCI system.
